subject.title: Feature: configurable LLM retry with backoff on transient errors (overloaded/529)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public configurable main-LLM retry/backoff policy, and should that policy live at provider scope, agent/global scope, or stay as built-in bounded retry behavior?
rationale: This adds new config surface in an auth/provider/fallback path where repository policy requires a high bar and maintainer intent before cementing a public contract.

options.title: Approve one retry contract
options.body: Pick one canonical provider or agent-level retry shape and require the implementation to cover schema, docs, runtime behavior, upgrade behavior, and focused tests before closing this issue.

options.title: Keep built-in only
options.body: Avoid a public retry knob for now and limit work to narrow built-in retry/fallback fixes such as idempotent same-model retries and cooldown handling.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave current manual retry/fallback behavior in place and close later only if maintainers decide the extra config surface is not worth carrying.

recommendation.title: Approve one retry contract
recommendation.body: Pick one canonical provider or agent-level retry shape and require the implementation to cover schema, docs, runtime behavior, upgrade behavior, and focused tests before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Current source routing and recent maintainer mention point to steipete as the best available owner for the provider/config product decision.
